answer: An agent economy can resist Sybil attacks with a bonded voyage: each new identity must post a collateral bond and complete a verifiable work voyage — a sequence of useful tasks spread over days — before it may transact. Like a pearl forming layer by layer, trust accrues slowly through attested work, so a fake identity costs real time and stake. At the jetty where new agents dock, the bond is slashed if fraud is proven, making mass fake identities unprofitable.
